# Brief

- Automatic project-memory reconciliation processes transcript ranges asynchronously, with transcript chunks capped at 96 KiB and provider requests capped at 64 KiB.
- Reconciliation filters secrets and instruction-injection text before provider requests.
- Project-memory prompt refresh replaces the owned memory block using its recorded character offset, length, and digest; it does not search flattened prompts for marker pairs. Sessions without the complete structured metadata remain unchanged.
- Automatic reconciliation prompts contain sanitized current memory files and serialized transcript rows. The runtime connects reconciliation to persisted activity and context preparation before eviction.
- Automatic memory reconciliation is the project mechanism for resolving conflicting memories and naturally deleting or superseding memories; an explicit `project_update` tool is not part of the current direction, and messaging-agent memory changes are expressed conversationally rather than through explicit forget requests.
- Gamma is treated as a subproject of Zeta. A useful Gamma project view would make project IDs, readable memory, memory history, related sessions, and inbox information easier to discover from the web frontend.
- Gamma's v0 architecture uses a FastAPI backend bound to `127.0.0.1`, REST endpoints for options and session views, and a per-session WebSocket at `/api/sessions/{id}/ws`; each Gamma session has one child process. The zeta read loop is the event pump, notifications carry cursors and publish timestamps, and reconnecting sockets replay buffered events from a supplied cursor. `zeta_protocol.py` is the sole wire-format boundary.
- The TUI role-color work preserves existing tool-card appearance as a project invariant; semantic colors distinguish agents, subagents, notices, warnings, successes, and errors without changing tool cards.
- Project inbox delivery uses one model-facing `inbox` tool with action-level policy and scoped subjects such as `send zeta`. Top-level sessions poll for new messages at startup, during idle periods, and after tool batches; changes produce durable notifications through TUI, turn-boundary, or existing serve notification paths. Child agents do not receive inbox access or polling, and inbox delivery has no daemon, network transport, ownership election, or per-message automatic model turn.
- On PR #368 head `ccf835aa01d392595834d3c4f282c3fba74d4e83`, automation delivery, failure, and interruption receipts and synthetic approval-anchor assistant records use `response_state="synthetic"`, so context eviction does not treat them as completed model replies; approval writes containing real completed model responses retain their normal state.
- PR #370's pushed repair uses sibling locking and atomic publication for machine-ID creation, unique temporary files, committed-ID rereads, `0600` permission repair, an explicit transport `machine_id`, and local/remote same-machine rejection; the repair is at `52538c4df9c947720e2352987e4765fe46a73f01` and was not merged or force-pushed in the reported validation.
- `zeta --computer` provides the model with a disposable Linux desktop and no host-computer file or command access; interaction is through screenshots, mouse, and keyboard control.
- Eviction markers are materialized snapshots rather than deltas; each later eviction can replace an earlier marker and write another full view.
- Admin-v3 PR #19246, `fix(v3-admin): wire harness compaction`, is merged. Jev fit v5 was evaluated on a Terra-labeled golden set with 50 cases, 3 repeats, $0.81 spend, and 0 failures; false abstentions fell from 268 in v2 to 5 in v5, and scoring without evidence fell from 71 to 16.
- The orchestrator control-panel direction favors a smooth experience with the same orchestrator behavior, one extra tool, and substantially freed context; orchestrators do not personally manage their lanes or debug a server, and the design avoids imposing a server-management burden on them.
- PR #390, merged as `ccdc9d62`, provides the v0 agent-attention panel: orchestrators use `request_attention`, `zeta panel` displays live orchestrators, child agents, and open attention items, and selecting an item opens a read/search-only discussion fork whose decision returns to the original orchestrator's inbox. Forks do not update memory or appear in project search.
- Discussion forks are excluded from ordinary project transcript search by one shared eligibility rule, while normal top-level, resumed, and session push/pull-derived sessions remain indexable. Fork allocation uses one `.fork-allocation.lock` per source session plus a brief directory lock for safe lock-file creation.
- PR #403 merged as `feea2084`. The delivery-ID feature supports durable idempotency IDs on `send` and `steer`, `delivery_status`, and terminal `dropped` delivery status; provider dispatch publication and outcome-based turn finalization prevent stale steering and duplicate history entries, while delivery-only memory ranges advance durable cursors without a model call.
- PR #405 merged into `main` as `93ab0e60`. Its evicted delivery-ID repair preserves a compact session-lifetime fingerprint and final outcome, distinguishes `evicted` from `unknown`, rejects reuse with error `-32010`, and reconstructs outcomes on restart; all four CI checks passed on the merge commit.
